text:
maya: heads up — started seeing occasional NaNs in long-seq paged-attn runs on dedicated tonight. only on fp8 profiles.
maya: repro via staging load with mixed batch sizes (1,4,8) and seq_len=12288. ~1 in 2000 requests.
liam: whoa. any stack traces?
maya: paste logs:
```
E GPU0: kernel fused_flash_attn_v2_fp8.cu: softmax returned inf/NaN at token 8192+
stack: runtime::dispatch -> attention::fused_attn_v2 -> softmax_fp8
```
sanjay: can you dump the logits before softmax (fp32) from that request?
maya: attached small dump (linked) — observed logits with peaks around 1e4 in some heads.
jen: weird — our fused kernel should be doing max-subtract for stability. maybe fp8 path bypassed that micro-optim? :thinking_face:  :eyes:  
liam: tag the commit that rolled yesterday? deploy-bot: deployed commit a7c2f9d (PR #1428) — kernel heuristics change: prefer fp8_paged for mixed-batch when avg_seq > 4096.
maya: that aligns. old heuristic picked bf16 for mixed batches.
sanjay: hypothesis: fp8_paged variant omitted max-subtract (or did it in fp8 quantized domain with insufficient headroom), causing exp overflow when logits have large magnitude; under mixed batches different head scaling triggers larger dot products.
liam: also saw kernel handoff inside the same CUDA launch when we batch different seq_lens — we switch kernel selection per microbatch which can cause suboptimal wavefront reuse and occasional precision regressions due to different accumulation order.
jen: reproduction script:
```bash
python -m bench.paged_attn --model llama-20b --dtype=fp8 --seq-len=12288 --batch-sizes 1 4 8 --iters 5000
```
liam: microprofile (nsight snippets):
```
sm_efficiency: 78%
warp_execution_efficiency: 62%
fp16_fma_throughput: 120 TFLOPS
mem_bandwidth_util: 82%
softmax_exp_rate: spiking before NaN events
```
maya: perf regression correlates with PR; before PR error rate ~0, after PR ~0.05%. throughput mostly same but tail latency increases on those NaNs (~5x).
sanjay: quick fixes to try: 1) implement stable softmax (max-subtract) in fp32 inside kernel before fp8 quantization; 2) clamp exp inputs to safe range; 3) if mixed-batch kernel handoff occurs, force single-kernel strategy per batch to avoid recompute ordering differences; 4) fallback to bf16 for sequences > 8192.
jen: agree. prioritize 1+3. clamping is bandaid. fallback to bf16 for very long seqs is reasonable short term.
liam: I ran a patch locally adding max-subtract in the fp32 path and it removed NaNs in 200k synthetic requests. microbench: -1.8% throughput on long sequences but no NaNs.
maya: can we gate the new behavior behind a runtime flag so we can ramp?
sanjay: yes — add config: `attention.stability.softmax_mode = "stable_fp32"|"fast_fp8"` default to stable_fp32 for dedicated until validated.
liam: also want to change kernel selection heuristic: prefer single-kernel per batch when seq_len variance > 50% to avoid mid-batch switches. reduces branch churn.
jen: test matrix:
- fp8_paged fast (current): run 1k requests, track NaN rate
- fp8_paged + max-subtract: same
- bf16_paged: baseline
- single-kernel forced: mixed batch vs uniform

maya: I'll run the matrix overnight on staging. attaching benchmark scripts to the PR.
liam: assign owner? sanjay take kernel changes, jen handle runtime flag + rollout gating, i'll own perf validation.
sanjay: taking it. will open a PR to add stable softmax in fp32 and a small fall-back in exp clamp with unit tests.
jen: i'll prepare a canary rollout policy: 10% dedicated, watch NaN metric + tail latency for 24h. deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for 2026-03-18T02:00Z (10% dedicated).
maya: thanks team. flagging for postmortem if canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
liam: FYI added a quick probe to console metrics: `redwood.attn.nan_events` and `redwood.attn.kernel_switch_count` — will graph.
maya: any other ideas?
sanjay: long-term: revisit fp8 quantization flow for softmax logits — maybe keep softmax in fp32 and only quantize outputs, or use dynamic range exp-scaling per head. both have perf tradeoffs.
jen: noted for Optimize roadmap.
liam: good work — appreciate quick triage. will post updates in this thread.
maya: update: stable_softmax patch + heuristic merged to staging branch, running overnight.
jen: :rocket:
perfb0t: perf snapshot: staging (stable_softmax): p50 latency +3%, p99 -25% (NaN eliminated), throughput -2% on 12k seq.
maya: closing for now, will reopen if we see more anomalies.
